Files.description: defines a file to write to a host.

data.description: holds inline content for the file, as an alternative to Source.

dst.description: is the path on the host where cargoship writes the file.

dstDir.description: is the directory on the host where cargoship writes the file.

group.description: identifies the file group on the host.

name.description: identifies the file in the cluster configuration.

perm.description: sets the file mode cargoship applies on the host.

src.description: is the local path or URL cargoship reads the file from.

user.description: identifies the file owner on the host.

FirewallConfig.description: is the backend-neutral firewall configuration for a node.

rules.description: lists the firewall rules cargoship applies to the node.

FirewallPolicyConfig.description: configures a firewalld policy that opens ports from one zone to another.

Egress.description: is the zone the policy allows traffic to.

Ingress.description: is the zone the policy allows traffic from.

ports.description: lists the ports this policy allows.

target.description: is the action taken on traffic that matches the policy.

FirewallPort.description: defines a port allowed through the firewalld policy.

port.description: is the port number, or port range, cargoship opens.

protocol.description: is the type of allowed traffic.

FirewallRule.description: is a single backend-neutral firewall rule.

action.description: is what cargoship does with traffic that matches the rule.

destination.description: is the address or CIDR the traffic goes to.

direction.description: selects which traffic the rule matches. It defaults to in.

egress.description:
names where forward traffic leaves. It is a zone on firewalld hosts and an
interface on ufw hosts. It applies to forward rules only.

ingress.description:
names where forward traffic enters. It is a zone on firewalld hosts and an
interface on ufw hosts. It applies to forward rules only.

name.description:
identifies the rule. Cargoship uses it to name the artifacts it writes on the
node, so it must be unique within a host. Cargoship generates one when it is empty.

port.description: is the port number, or inclusive port range, the rule matches.

protocol.description: is the type of traffic the rule matches.

source.description: is the address or CIDR the traffic comes from.

FirewallZone.description: is the name of either the ingress or egress zone for a policy.

HostConfig.description: defines the configuration for a specific host, including firewall policies and the ports cargoship opens on the node.

firewall.description:
holds the backend-neutral firewall rules cargoship renders onto whichever
firewall the node runs, firewalld, ufw, or nftables.

policy.description:
maps a policy name to a firewalld policy that allows traffic from one interface to another.
It is firewalld-only; prefer forward rules under `firewall.rules` for new configuration.

ports.description: lists the ports and protocols cargoship opens on the node.

HostEngine.description: defines configuration options for node-level metadata, specifically Kubernetes node labels and taints applied to a cluster host.

labels.description: maps Kubernetes node label keys to their values.

taints.description: lists the Kubernetes node taints cargoship applies to the node.

HostPort.description: is a port cargoship opens on the public side of the firewall.

port.description: is the port number, or port range, cargoship opens.

protocol.description: is the type of allowed traffic.

Profiles.description: holds the host and engine overrides for one profile.

concurrency.description:
limits how many hosts using this profile cargoship processes at once, e.g.
draining, upgrading, initializing, or uninstalling. It accepts a fixed count ("1") or a
percentage of the hosts sharing this profile ("25%"). Empty falls back to the phase's
default concurrency.

engine.description: holds the node label and taint overrides applied to a host that selects this profile.

host.description: holds the configuration overrides applied to a host that selects this profile.

inherit.description: names another profile this one starts from. The settings here win, and anything this profile leaves empty is taken from the named one, which may itself inherit. Without it a cluster whose profiles differ in one field each has to spell every one of them out in full, which is how a profiles block grows faster than the fleet does.

address.description: Address of the remote host (IP or hostname)

ignoreSSHConfig.description: Do not read ~/.ssh/config or the system ssh_config for this host

options.description: Additional SSH options as ssh_config key-value pairs

description: is the set of Ansible variables cargoship reads for one host, as a type, so that a JSON Schema can be generated from it and an editor can complete and check a host_vars or group_vars file.

ansible_host.description: Address cargoship opens the SSH connection to. Defaults to the name the inventory knows the host by, which is the common shape.

ansible_port.description: Port cargoship connects on. Defaults to 22.

ansible_ssh_private_key_file.description: Path to the SSH private key cargoship authenticates with.

ansible_user.description: User cargoship connects as. Defaults to root.

cargoship_bastion.description: Jump host cargoship reaches this node through. Cargoship does not parse ansible_ssh_common_args, so an inventory that reaches the fleet through a bastion for Ansible's own sake has to say so again here.

cargoship_environment.description: Shell environment cargoship sets on the host, as a map of variable name to value.

cargoship_files.description: Each entry is a file cargoship uploads to the host: src is a path on the management node, dst the path on the node.

cargoship_host.description: Ports cargoship opens on this node, and the firewall rules it applies there.

cargoship_hostname.description: What the node calls itself, when that is not the name the inventory knows it by. Defaults to the inventory hostname.

cargoship_node_labels.description: Kubernetes node labels applied to this node. A host setting this replaces its group's rather than adding to it.

cargoship_node_taints.description: Kubernetes node taints applied to this node. A host setting this replaces its group's rather than adding to it.

cargoship_private_address.description: Address the cluster uses between nodes, when it is not the one cargoship would discover. A node with two interfaces is the usual reason.

cargoship_private_interface.description: Interface the cluster uses between nodes, when it is not the one cargoship would discover.

cargoship_profile.description: Name of the profile this host selects. Defaults to the host's role, which is what makes the node-role.kubernetes.io/<profile> label say something.

cargoship_profile_spec.description: Body of the profile this host selects, declared beside the selection. A profile defined twice with different bodies is an error naming both sources.
